thread:
sanjay: quick heads-up — polestar int6 bring-up looked OK perf-wise but QA found a regression on our multilingual recall set, especially at k=5. posting numbers.
embed-eval-bot: [AUTO] polestar-int6 | evalset: langmix-holdout | recall@1: 0.842 -> 0.813 (-2.9%) | recall@5: 0.942 -> 0.878 (-6.4%) | mean_norm: 1.02 -> 0.79 (-22.5%) | silhouette: 0.14 -> 0.08 (-0.06) | n=12,480
maria: ugh. is that whitened vs unwhitened? also which calibration method for int6? (per-tensor/per-channel?)
embed-eval-bot: details: quant_mode=int6_perchannel, calib_samples=1024, seq_len=256, fp16 baseline used.
oliver: my first suspect is LN folding / bias folding changed distribution. big drop in mean_norm suggests effective scale change; could be accenting rare tokens in some langs.
jess: can we re-run with whiten and with per-channel+overflow clipping? try calib_samples=4096 and include longer examples (seq 512). I can start a run now.
maria: paste the command so i can mirror it locally
sanjay: here — ./tools/embed_eval --model polestar/int6-perchannel --calib 4096 --seq 512 --dataset langmix-holdout --whiten True --batch 128 --save-umap run/1778503210
maria: running locally, will post quick stats when done. :eyes:
embed-eval-bot: queued run 1778503210-1 (whiten=True, calib=4096)
jess: also add --norm-check to output per-lang mean norms, and --k=1,5,10
maria: quick result (whiten on, calib 4k): recall@1 0.839 (-0.3%), recall@5 0.918 (-2.5%), mean_norm 0.98 (close to fp16), silhouette 0.12. so whiten helped but not fully recovered to baseline.
oliver: interesting — whiten mitigated centroid shift but still delta at k=5. maybe cluster compactness for low-resource langs still worse. did we include english-heavy calibration data? could bias calibration toward en tokens.
sanjay: calibration corpus was the default multilingual sampler — might be skewed. next: run stratified calibration per-lang and try per-channel with symmetric/asymmetric clipping.
jess: while that's running, check kmeans inertia and top-k confusions. small drop in recall@5 could be due to small leaderboard anchors moving — e.g. top-5 borderline examples flipping.
maria: pasted top confusions (excerpt):
```
query: "¿Cuál es la capital de Perú?"
fp16 top5: [Lima, Quito, Santiago, Bogota, La Paz]
int6 top5: [Lima, Quito, La Paz, Santiago, Guayaquil]
```
maria: seems position swap among nearby latam capitals — borderline distance jitter.
oliver: that pattern matches quantization noise around tokens with diacritics — embedding subvectors for accented chars might have higher quantization error. try calibration that over-samples languages with diacritics and longer tails.
sanjay: agree. also file a quick checklist: 1) per-lang stratified calib (4k each) 2) compare int6_perchannel symmetric vs asymmetric 3) generate UMAP diff images + per-lang mean_norm table 4) run kmeans silhouette per-lang
jess: i started stratified run: ./tools/embed_eval --model polestar/int6-perchannel --calib-split stratified --calib-per-lang 4096 --seq 512 --whiten True --norm-check --save-umap run/1778503210-strat
embed-eval-bot: queued run 1778503210-strat (ETA ~45m)
maria: tiny note — the runtime inference KV cache isn't used in eval harness, does production runtime do any prefix caching that could affect norms? we should test with cached prefix lengths 16/64.
oliver: good call — if runtime folding or prefix-attn optimizations change token cooccurrence, distribution can shift. add prefix_cache_len=64 test.
sanjay: putting brief triage summary in ticket INF-2337: polestar int6 onboard — recall@5 drop (-6.4%) mitigated by whitening and larger calib; suspected causes: calibration skew, accent token quant noise, LN folding. next steps assigned to @maria for stratified calib, @jess for per-channel mode comparisons, @oliver to check LN folding diffs. :thumbsup:
maria: ok i'll update INF-2337 with strat runs and attach UMAPs when ready.
jess: will post per-channel vs per-tensor diffs once runs finish.
embed-eval-bot: [AUTO] run 1778503210-strat completed | recall@1 0.841 | recall@5 0.937 | mean_norm 1.01 | silhouette 0.13
sanjay: nice, stratified calib nearly restores baseline. looks like production recommendation: keep int6_perchannel but require stratified calibration + whiten by default for multilingual onboarding. will draft a short onboarding note.
maria: drafting note now, will ping for review. :coffee:
